title: Count 5 Floors Outside — There Are 9 Inside | China Travel Expert
description:
The Sakyamuni Pagoda of Fogong Temple in Yingxian, Shanxi, was finished in 1056. It is 67.31 m of timber with no steel, no concrete, and no metal nails in its joints — and it is still the tallest wooden pagoda in the world (Guinness certified it in September 2016).

From outside you count five storeys and six rings of eaves. Inside there are nine levels: between every visible floor sits a low hidden one. Those four hidden levels are packed with diagonal timber braces that work like modern trusses, making a stiff belt around the tower.

Four things keep it standing:
1) Interlocking bracket sets (dougong) — 50+ types on this one building. Under shaking the blocks rotate and the arms slide, and that friction burns off the quake's energy.
2) Two rings of columns — eight inner, twenty-four outer — tied together so the octagon works as one stiff tube inside a tube.
3) Four hidden floors bracing the structure like trusses.
4) The whole tower sways and twists instead of snapping.

The diagrams here are drawn in code by us (schematic, not to scale) — no AI imagery. The opening and closing shots are a real licensed photo of the pagoda.

应县木塔，建于1056年，高67.31米，木结构、榫卯、关节不用铁钉。外面看五层，里面其实九层——四个暗层里全是斜撑，像现代桁架一样箍住整座塔。
